medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The School of Medicine encourages applications from persons from groups underrepresented in medicine. The School of Medicine has an NIH-funded Center for Health Disparities and Molecular Medicine. The School of Medicine's Center for Health Disparities and the Dean's Office sponsor pipeline programs to increase the number of underrepresented students.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A student may apply for a leave of absence through the School of Medicine's Offices of Educational Affairs and Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
The purpose of the Loma Linda University School of Medicine student organizations is to create an avenue through which students may work with school administration and faculty to enhance their educational experience and further the mission of the school.  These organizations also add to the medical school experience by organizing social, spiritual and service activities and engaging students in issues related to medical education and health care through participation in regional and national professional organizations. School of Medicine student organizations include chapters of the American Medical Association and California Medical Association, the Student National Medical Association, the American Medical Women's Association, and the Latino Medical Student Association.  There are also active student interest groups for the various medical specialties.  

At registration, students automatically become members of the Loma Linda University School of Medicine Student Association.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Loma Linda is located in the Inland Empire region of Southern California, equidistant between Los Angeles and Palm Springs.  The community is bordered on the north by the San Bernardino mountains which provide opportunity for both winter and summer recreation.  The Pacific Ocean beaches are approximately an hour's drive away.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: The University owns and operates residence halls for men and women.  Space is limited, but there is ample housing available for rent in the community.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The University has an official club for LGBTQ students and a resource site that provides groups, mental health support, and a list of educational and community support resources for LGBTQ students.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: It is the students’ responsibility to have access to transportation for off-campus assignments and, if driving, maintain a valid driver’s license.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Dress code requirements are outlined in the Student Handbook provided at orientation and available online.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Office of Student Affairs coordinates a peer-tutoring program and assists students who request academic coaching from learning specialists and faculty.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: In every year of medical school
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Pedagogy is balanced between lecture and a variety of active learning modalities.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Students may rotate through multiple hospitals: university tertiary care hospital, Veteran's Administration hospital, Midwest teaching hospital, urban teaching hospital, county hospitals, and others.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is required at all team-based learning and interactive sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The School of Medicine seeks to prepare students who will be well grounded in the science and art of medicine. The pre-clerkship phase of the curriculum utilizes an organ systems-based approach to the study of the biomedical sciences and their application to clinical medicine.  The pre-clerkship curriculum is divided between traditional lecture and a variety of active learning modalities, including small group and independent learning activities that prepare students to be effective lifelong learners. The clerkship phase of the curriculum provides clinical rotations in the major areas of medical practice. Elective time is available for additional experience in clinical or research areas. Qualified students interested in a career in academic medicine may earn an M.S. or Ph.D. degree along with the M.D. degree in a total of six to eight years.  Third-year students have the opportunity to distinguish themselves by earning high pass or honors in their clerkships.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Over 40% of Loma Linda University School of Medicine graduates enter primary care residencies.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The Office of Student Affairs coordinates a research program for students during the summer following their first year of medicine and provides a stipend to assist with cost of living.  More than 70 students participate in this program annually.  Students may arrange to participate in research projects at other times during medical school years as their schedules allow.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: There is a service learning requirement of 20 hours for each student. Ample local and international service learning opportunities are provided.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Research opportunities are available to students, including a funded summer research opportunity following the freshman year.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Loma Linda University Medical Center, Children's Hospital, and Behavioral Medicine Center; VA Loma Linda Healthcare; 6 area hospitals/medical centers; and 1 hospital each in Florida, Ohio, and Oregon.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/Fail; third-year students may distinguish themselves by earning high pass or honors in their clerkships.
medSchoolCurriculum.languageInstructions: English; therefore, proficiency in spoken and written English is required.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
We have educated medical students in a supportive Christian environment of excellence and caring since 1909. Our process has followed the best practices of medical education throughout its history while holding true to the original mission, to “continue the teaching and healing ministry of Jesus Christ to make man whole.” 

We have two faith-based regional campuses: AdventHealth Orlando Campus (Florida) and Kettering Health Campus (Ohio). Students train at main campus in Southern California for the first two years followed by clinical training at regional campuses for the last two years. A tuition incentive may be available. AdventHealth Orlando: tertiary and quaternary system serving patients from the Southeast, the Caribbean, and Latin America. Kettering Health: tertiary system serving patients from urban, suburban, and rural communities. *Selecting a regional campus on the secondary application is binding. https://medicine.llu.edu/admissions/medicine-md-program/regional-campuses
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The mission of the School of Medicine is to continue the teaching and healing ministry of Jesus Christ. Our overriding purpose is to foster the formation of Christian physicians, providing whole-person care to individuals, families, and communities. Fulfilling this responsibility requires education, research, service, developing the whole person, and reaching the world.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Letters of evaluation are required of all applicants and must be submitted to AMCAS.

If the pre-health professions advising office at the applicant's school provides a committee recommendation or a packet of recommendations, this committee recommendation or packet is required by the School of Medicine and no other recommendations are required.

If the applicant's school does not provide a committee recommendation or packet, a minimum of three and maximum of six recommendation letters from individuals who know the applicant well are required. At least one of those recommendations must be from a science professor who has taught the applicant. It is suggested that the other references come from a physician whom you have shadowed, an employer, your pastor or other clergy, or a leader in your volunteering experiences.

Applications are not considered complete until receipt of all letters of recommendation the applicant has indicated to expect in AMCAS and our minimum has been met.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Applicants will participate in two separate one-on-one virtual interviews for 30-40 minutes each. Opportunity to view a virtual tour of campus is provided.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two separate one-on-one interviews with a combination of clinical faculty, basic sciences faculty, residents, medical students, or administrators.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Applicants accepted through the Early Decision Program have demonstrated excellence in academics, MCAT, extracurriculars, premed core competencies, and mission alignment.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: There is no preference between in-state or out-of-state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Preference for admission is given to academically -qualified, mission-aligned members of the Seventh-day Adventist Church.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
For admission, applicants are expected to obtain a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university in the United States or Canada prior to matriculation.  The degree can be in any field of study with the recommendation that the applicant advance beyond the basic courses of the chosen field.  No preference is given for either science or non-science majors; however, increased coursework in the sciences beyond the basic requirements has been found to be beneficial in the preparation of an applicant for medical school.  A curriculum that includes the study of humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences is recommended to provide a solid preparation for the MCAT, medical school, and the future role as a physician.
Pass/Fail – Accepted for prerequisite coursework taken during the winter/spring 2020 academic terms only.

medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Application updates may be submitted after submission of the secondary application by uploading the update to the portal at medapp.llu.edu. Typical updates include activities, letters of interest, and unofficial transcripts. Changes in contact information must be submitted to AMCAS prior to emailing the changes to our office.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The majority of students in the School of Medicine fund their education through federal financial aid.  All aid is awarded on the basis of a standardized need analysis formula.  Students may finance their education with need and non-need based assistance.  Financial aid information is provided to all accepted students.  To meet the costs of a medical education, students are encouraged to consider all of their financing options and budget accordingly.  Please contact the Office of Financial Aid for more information.

medSchoolPrograms.info: The Medical Scientist Program (MSP) at Loma Linda University is designed to attract those students who are energized by doing biomedical research and wish to contribute substantially to this enterprise. The expectation is that graduates of this program will pursue a career in academic medicine and medical research. The program integrates graduate and medical education in a Christian environment and is designed to allow completion of both the PhD and MD degrees. *Please note: MD/PhD students start with the first two years of medical school, followed by the PhD program, and then back to medical school for the remaining two years.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The Admissions Committee determines which applicants are placed on the waitlist.  Waitlist acceptances are offered as seats become available in the class, but no later than first day of Orientation.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
It is expected that all applicants for admission complete a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university in the United States or Canada.

Our admissions requirements are in place to aid the applicant in preparation for the MCAT and to provide a strong foundation in the sciences for medical school coursework. CLEP and pass/fail credits are not accepted in fulfillment of the required prerequisite courses. A full year sequence (generally two semesters or three quarters) of each prerequisite is required. One academic term of biochemistry is also required. R

Additionally, regardless of academic degree, advanced coursework in the sciences and mathematics provides outstanding preparation of applicants to medical school and should be electively pursued whenever possible.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No expiration date for prerequisite coursework; however, current knowledge in the sciences is expected for potential success on the MCAT and preparedness for rigorous medical school coursework.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Admissions Committee seeks applicants who demonstrate the greatest potential for becoming capable physicians. A strong academic background is needed in preparation for medical studies. Particular attention is given to performance in science courses, but a solid foundation in the humanities, social sciences, and human behavior is also expected. Selections are made based on overall scholastic record and MCAT score, personal characteristics, premed core competencies, and commitment to medicine and the school's mission.  The School of Medicine is owned and operated by the Seventh-day Adventist Church. Preference for admission is given to academically qualified and mission aligned members; however, it is a firm policy of the Admissions Committee to admit applicants from other faiths who have not only demonstrated a strong commitment to Christian principles, but also have the best potential of fulfilling our mission. No applicant is accepted based on religious affiliation alone.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Applicants are required to obtain physician shadowing experience and direct patient care exposure to better inform their decision for a career in medicine.
